quotes.text:
/**
 * Compare two messages for ordering their rows.
 *
 * @typedef {Function} Comparator
 * @param {Message} a - A message object.
 * @param {Message} b - A message object.
 * @returns {boolean} - True if message A should be above message B.
 */

/**
 * Get a comparator that can be used to put messages in alphabetical order.
 *
 * @param {string} property - The message property to be used for ordering.
 * @returns {Comparator} - A function that accepts two messages, A and B, and
 *   returns true if message A is ahead of message B in the alphabet.
 */
function getTextComparator(property) {
  return (a, b) => lazy.collator.compare(a[property], b[property]) < 0;
}

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The adapter comparator answers whether message A belongs above message B. getTextComparator converts the collator result to a boolean with < 0; descending order swaps arguments before calling the predicate. This is not the negative/zero/positive callback contract of Array.sort. Preserve the return type and argument-order meaning in helpers and JSDoc. Accepted collator construction no longer contains the original sensitivity: base option. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Document this comparator as a boolean ordering predicate
